summary:
The FAFSA Deadline Act, Pub. L. 118-145, amends section 483(d)(4) of the Higher Education Act of 1965, 20 U.S.C. 1090(d)(4), to require an earlier and fixed annual application processing cycle for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid.

Section 2 amends 20 U.S.C. 1090(d)(4) by replacing the prior timing standard—under which the Secretary of Education was to enable application submission “not later than January 1” of the applicant’s planned year of enrollment and, “to the maximum extent practicable,” on or around the preceding October 1—with a mandatory deadline requiring availability “not later than October 1 prior to the applicant’s planned year of enrollment.” This converts the October 1 target into the operative statutory deadline and removes the January 1 outer deadline and practicability qualifier.

Section 3 further amends the same paragraph by redesignating the existing Secretary obligation as subparagraph (A), captioned “In general,” and adding a new subparagraph (B), captioned “Certification and testimony requirements.” For each application processing cycle, before initiation of that cycle, the Secretary must, not later than September 1, certify to the authorizing committees either that the Department of Education will meet the October 1 deadline specified in subparagraph (A) or that it will not meet that deadline. If the Secretary certifies that the Department will not meet the deadline, the Secretary must, not later than September 30, testify before the authorizing committees regarding the anticipated failure to meet the deadline and the financial impact that failure will have on students and families.

The Act contains no authorization of appropriations, appropriation, sunset provision, or express delayed effective date.
